glossary.Cardiac output: The volume of blood the heart pumps each minute.
glossary.Circulation: Movement of blood around the body.
glossary.Myocardial infarction: A heart attack: death of heart muscle from a blocked coronary artery.
glossary.Electrolyte imbalance: Abnormal blood levels of salts such as potassium, calcium or magnesium.
glossary.Drug overdose: Taking more of a drug than the body can safely handle.
glossary.Unresponsive: Not reacting to voice or pain.
glossary.Palpable pulse: A pulse that can be felt with the fingers.
glossary.QRS: The ECG complex from ventricular depolarisation; broad in VT.
glossary.SVT: Supraventricular tachycardia: a fast rhythm starting above the ventricles.
glossary.Hypoxia: Low oxygen levels in the tissues.
glossary.Metabolic disturbance: Abnormal body chemistry, such as abnormal calcium, glucose or acidosis.
glossary.Toxins: Poisons or drugs taken in overdose.
glossary.Thrombosis: A blood clot blocking a vessel, here a PE or coronary artery.
glossary.PE: Pulmonary embolism: a clot blocking the arteries of the lungs.
glossary.ALS algorithm: The Resuscitation Council step-by-step guide to advanced resuscitation.
glossary.Defibrillator: A machine that reads the heart rhythm and delivers an electric shock.
glossary.Unsynchronised shock: A shock given at any point in the cycle, used in VF and pulseless VT.
glossary.J: Joules: the unit of energy for a defibrillator shock.
glossary.Proximal humerus: The top end of the upper arm bone, near the shoulder.
glossary.Proximal tibia: The top end of the shin bone, just below the knee.
glossary.Distal tibia: The lower end of the shin bone, near the ankle.
glossary.Wide-bore cannula: A large-diameter plastic tube inserted through the skin.
glossary.2nd intercostal space: The gap between the 2nd and 3rd ribs, used for needle decompression.
glossary.Coronary perfusion: Blood flow through the coronary arteries to the heart muscle.
glossary.Depolarise: Make the cell membrane's charge less negative so the cell fires.
glossary.Ischaemic heart disease: Narrowing of the coronary arteries reducing blood supply to the heart muscle.
glossary.Pacemaker: The part of the heart that sets its rhythm, normally the SA node.
glossary.Mechanical contraction: The physical squeezing of the heart muscle that pumps blood.
glossary.Peripheral vasoconstriction: Narrowing of blood vessels in the limbs and skin, pushing blood to the core organs.
glossary.Antiarrhythmic: A drug that treats or prevents abnormal heart rhythms.
glossary.Action potential: The electrical impulse that travels across a heart cell when it fires.
glossary.Resuscitation: Emergency treatment to restart the heart and breathing.
glossary.Compression-to-ventilation ratio: The number of chest compressions given for each set of rescue breaths.
